objection_handlers.q: Algolia's sub-50ms global latency is a hard requirement.
objection_handlers.a: Elastic Cloud regional clusters plus searchable snapshots and HTTP-level caching match the latency budget for the regions that matter. Round-trip within region is comparable.

objection_handlers.q: We do not have search engineers; Algolia is fully managed.
objection_handlers.a: Elastic Cloud Serverless and Search Applications give the same managed surface. The investment is one-time and pays back at renewal scale.

pricing_anchor: Algolia Premium lists at $1.50 per 1000 records/month plus $0.50 per 1000 search requests. See algolia.com/pricing.
gotchas: For small catalogs (under 1M records), Algolia's per-record pricing is competitive and the time-to-launch is unbeatable.
Algolia's merchandising UI for non-engineers is more polished than Elastic Search Applications today.
Algolia's NeuralSearch is a strong managed semantic-search experience for teams that do not want to model relevance.
Algolia's CDN-style global edge serving is very mature; Elastic edge story is region-based plus customer-managed CDNs.

What other data could share the same search cluster (orders, sessions, logs)?
What is your Algolia renewal date and current monthly run-rate?
clincher: Algolia is rented search. Elastic is owned search on the data plane your business already runs on.

tagline: Open relevance plus open data, on the same platform that runs your logs and SIEM
key_pain: Coveo's enterprise relevance and recommendations are mature and well-tuned for Salesforce and ServiceNow shops. The cost: a closed ML stack, indexed-document pricing, and a single-purpose footprint that does not extend to RAG, log analytics, observability or security.

talking_points.claim: ELSER, dense vectors, the inference API and external model integrations are open and inspectable.
talking_points.proof: Coveo's relevance and Coveo ML run inside Coveo's tenant; export and portability are limited. Elastic detection rules, ML jobs and inference pipelines are open and Git-managed.

talking_points.claim: Per-GB ingest plus tiered storage instead of indexed-document tiers.
talking_points.proof: Coveo prices per indexed document and per query class; large catalogs and high-traffic sites hit pricing inflection. Elastic decouples ingest from storage cost.

talking_points.claim: The same cluster runs site search, RAG, observability and security.
talking_points.proof: Coveo is search-and-recommendations only. Elastic consolidates 3-4 stacks at the next renewal cycle.

tagline: Elastic shipped the platform features Solr-based Fusion is still chasing
key_pain: Lucidworks Fusion is the commercial wrapper around Apache Solr, with strong relevance heritage and a deep services practice. talking_points.claim: Elastic ships major capability every 6 to 8 weeks and powers Beats, Agent and the wider OTel community.

talking_points.claim: ELSER sparse plus dense plus BM25 with RRF in one query, plus the inference API for any external model.

talking_points.claim: Same cluster runs RAG, observability, APM and security.

tagline: Falcon catches the endpoint. Elastic catches the rest and keeps the history.
key_pain: CrowdStrike Falcon dominates endpoint detection and response. talking_points.claim: Frozen tier on object storage gives 12-24+ months of searchable retention at object-storage prices.
talking_points.proof: Falcon LogScale (ex-Humio) retention is priced per GB ingest plus storage tier; Elastic searchable snapshots on S3/GCS/Azure Blob are typically cheaper at the 12-month boundary.

talking_points.claim: Detection rules in EQL, KQL or ES|QL, all open-source on GitHub at elastic/detection-rules with full CI.

Falcon LogScale's real-time search on small windows is genuinely fast and well-loved.
CrowdStrike's threat-intel and managed-hunting (Falcon OverWatch and Complete) are mature commercial offerings with deep telemetry depth.
If the customer does not need cross-domain correlation or long retention, Falcon Insight plus Next-Gen SIEM may be enough.

tagline: S1 stops the host. Elastic is the open SIEM that hunts across everything else.
key_pain: SentinelOne Singularity is a strong autonomous EDR with mature one-click rollback. Its SIEM and data lake story (Singularity Data Lake, ex-Scalyr) is newer; long retention and broad detection content outside the endpoint are less mature than the established SIEM market.

talking_points.claim: Elastic ingests SentinelOne agent telemetry and alerts via the documented integration; Elastic Security correlates across identity, network and cloud.
talking_points.proof: The Elastic SentinelOne integration ships in Fleet with ECS mappings. Customers keep S1 on the endpoint and run Elastic as the SIEM and hunt platform.

talking_points.claim: Frozen tier on object storage gives 12-24+ months of searchable retention at object-storage prices.
talking_points.proof: Singularity Data Lake retention is priced per GB ingest plus tier; Elastic searchable snapshots on S3/GCS/Azure Blob are typically cheaper at the 12-month boundary.

talking_points.claim: Detection rules in EQL, KQL or ES|QL on GitHub with full CI; rule IP stays with the customer.
talking_points.proof: S1's STAR rules are powerful but proprietary. Elastic detection rules are AGPLv3 and Git-managed, including in air-gapped deployments.

elastic_advantages: Native SentinelOne integration ingests alerts, agents and threats
Frozen tier on object storage for SIEM-class retention
Open detection rule format on GitHub (elastic/detection-rules)
MITRE ATT&CK navigator built into Kibana
Cross-domain correlation across endpoint, identity, network and cloud
Self-hosted, Elastic Cloud or air-gapped deployment

proof_points.metric: Elastic SentinelOne integration is documented and ECS-mapped.
Elastic detection-rules repository is public on GitHub with full CI.
SentinelOne Singularity Core list pricing is published around $45/endpoint/year for the entry tier.
proof_points.source: Public SentinelOne pricing references; see sentinelone.com/platform-packages for current bundles

objection_handlers.q: Singularity Data Lake is included in the platform; why pay for a second SIEM?
objection_handlers.a: SDL ingest, retention pricing and detection content depth are still maturing relative to the established SIEM market. Run a like-for-like POV on detection coverage and 12-month retention TCO before assuming the bundle wins.

objection_handlers.q: S1's autonomous rollback and quarantine are best-in-class.
objection_handlers.a: We agree on the endpoint. The pitch is not to replace S1; it is to be the SIEM that consumes S1 telemetry, retains long, and correlates with non-endpoint domains.

objection_handlers.q: We already pay for SDL; doubling on SIEM is hard to justify.
objection_handlers.a: Compare 12 and 24-month retention TCO side by side at full ingest. Frozen tier on object storage typically wins materially; SDL value is short-window real-time search.

pricing_anchor: SentinelOne Singularity Core entry tier is roughly $45/endpoint/year list; Control and Complete bundles are higher and quote-based. Verify on sentinelone.com/platform-packages.
gotchas: On autonomous EDR remediation and rollback, S1 is best-in-class; do not pretend otherwise.
Singularity Identity (post-Attivo) gives strong identity-attack telemetry that Elastic ingests but does not generate.
Vigilance MDR is a mature managed-hunting service with deep S1 product knowledge.
For mid-market customers without a separate SIEM team, the bundle convenience can win on simplicity even if TCO is higher long-term.

Where do non-endpoint detections live: identity, network, cloud, application logs?
Who writes and maintains your detection content?
What is the Vigilance MDR scope, and is it adequate for the broader SOC mission?
clincher: S1 ends the attack on the host. Elastic remembers it long enough to find the next one.

tagline: Snowflake is the warehouse; Elastic is the real-time search and observability layer on top of it
key_pain: Snowflake is excellent at structured analytics on cold data but expensive and slow for ad-hoc text search, log tail latency, and operational dashboards. Customers pipe logs into Snowflake for retention and then realize they still need an interactive search/SIEM layer for SOC and SRE workflows.

talking_points.claim: Sub-second log search and dashboard refresh; Snowflake virtual warehouses spin up in seconds and bill per query.
talking_points.proof: Elastic hot tier serves p95 < 1s for typical SOC queries. Snowflake compute warm-up plus credit burn make per-incident pivoting cost-prohibitive.

talking_points.claim: ECS plus runtime fields keep unstructured logs queryable without pre-modeling.
talking_points.proof: Snowflake requires schema definition and VARIANT parsing for JSON; Elastic indexes any document and lets ES|QL or Lucene queries hit it immediately.

talking_points.claim: Detection rules, APM, RUM, ML anomaly detection ship out of the box - no SQL workbench to build them in.
talking_points.proof: Snowflake needs Sigma, Hunters, Panther or a custom dbt stack on top to become a SIEM. Elastic Security is the product.

elastic_advantages: Real-time ingest and search latency that Snowflake cannot match for log tails
Frozen tier on object storage for cheap long retention alongside hot search
Built-in SIEM, APM, RUM, ML on the same index - no separate analytics stack
Vector search and ELSER for RAG over the same logs without moving data
Open ECS schema and ES|QL; no per-query credit billing

common_objections.q: We already have a Snowflake commit; everything goes there.
common_objections.a: Keep Snowflake for warehouse analytics. Elastic sits in front for the sub-second log search and SIEM workflows Snowflake is not built for. Many customers run both: Elastic for hot operational data, Snowflake for cold structured analytics.

common_objections.q: Snowflake Cortex and notebooks give us AI on our data.
common_objections.a: Cortex is excellent for SQL-shaped analytics. Elastic's inference API plus ELSER plus hybrid retrieval is purpose-built for unstructured text and is what SREs and SOC analysts actually run against logs in seconds.

common_objections.q: Why pay for another platform when Snowflake retains everything?
common_objections.a: The bill comparison usually flips when you count Snowflake credits burned by interactive log searches and dashboard refreshes. Elastic hot plus frozen tiers on object storage land cheaper at the access pattern SREs and SOCs actually use.

discovery_questions: Are your SREs and SOC analysts querying Snowflake live, or do they have a separate operational tool?
What does Snowflake credit burn look like for ad-hoc log search and dashboard refresh?
Where does your incident response runbook expect sub-second pivots across logs, traces and identity?
What is your retention requirement and what mix of hot versus cold do you actually need?
clincher: Snowflake stores it. Elastic searches it.
